verdict.english_script:
HR rejects all CVs like these.
I mean these really graphic, fancy ones.
So in 2026 you can't expect to find work with CVs like these.
A good CV should look like this: really boring and professional.
ATS filters go through the CVs, and ATS is a machine that weeds out the bad CVs.
My best friend works in HR, and she tipped me off about this really good site.
It's jobstep.io.
You just upload your CV there, it analyzes it, and right away you see a score and an assessment of your CV.
Here.
And if your score is under 50, your CV gets rejected automatically by the ATS filter.
Luckily you can improve it here, step by step.
We go through every step, and here you edit the layout, formatting, work experience and education.
At the end you can switch the template here, and I'm trying to pick the most minimalist one, so it fits really well.

verdict.english_script:
This one gets rejected, this one gets rejected, and this one gets rejected three times.
This one doesn't get rejected.
And why?
People, in 2026 you can't send in CVs like these anymore.
These aren't ATS-proof at all; they have icons and charts that an ATS system can't read.
This CV, on the other hand, is in the right format, the ATS format recruiters want to see, even though these ones are much prettier.
And how do you make a CV like this?
You make it with a tool, for example Jobstep.io.
It asks you a whole bunch of questions about your personal experience, all based on the job posting, and then builds an ATS-proof CV for you.
One like this one here.
And if you want, you can also change the design here, the template and colors, and even the whole layout, so you can customize your CV a bit.

verdict.english_script:
I'm leaving my Human Resources job, and now I can tell you for sure why they're not hiring you.
And the problem with all of this is the Canva templates you use, uhm, the Canva templates.
As soon as we saw a Canva-style CV, we threw it out.
We didn't even read it.
Why?
Because they don't pass the ATS filters.
Basically, companies use this ATS filter, a piece of software, to save time: instead of going through them one by one, they run them through this system.
If they see lots of little drawings, pretty designs, etc., an "aesthetic design" so to speak, they throw it out immediately.
So basically, don't put a lot of effort into making a "pretty" CV, because here it doesn't matter if it's pretty; what matters is that it passes the ATS filters.
Basically you have to make a simple CV, but don't worry, I'm your savior and I'm going to show you how to do it.
[Go to the] job you want and copy the link.
Then you go to this app called Jobstep.io.
We paste the link into this same app and click "Add job".
Right away it generates a CV and a cover letter for us.
And here it takes us to our CV, which is the important part.
It passes the ATS filters.
And as you can see, here we already have our CV that fits the job we want perfectly.

verdict.english_script:
This CV got rejected, and this one, and this one too.
And only now did I find out why: these kinds of CVs never even reach recruiters.
Because when you send a CV to a company, it first goes through ATS filters.
And if the CV doesn't get past these ATS filters, nobody ever reads it.
So you need a CV that's compatible with these filters.
And I'm going to show you right now what I used to improve my CV.
You need to go to the jobse.io website, and then add the link to a job you want.
You can find one on eJobs or LinkedIn, or lots of other platforms.
Then it helps us edit our CV so it's as compatible as possible with the job we added.
And you just have to talk to the chat.
As you can see, I have a 68% match with the job.
And the more you edit it, the higher the score goes.
verdict.hook_en: This CV got rejected, and this one, and this one too. And only now did I find out why: these kinds of CVs never even reach recruiters.
verdict.reason: Like N10, the creator flips through several of their own rejected CVs, explains that ATS filters stop them before any recruiter reads them, and then demos the tool that makes an ATS-compatible CV. The archived ESX21, which shows several designed CVs that ATS rejects, is the same premise.

verdict.english_script:
I recently got out of unemployment, so I'm going to give you a tip so you can get out of it too.
I always applied to a ton of jobs, but none of them took me.
And that's because I used those typical Canva CVs that I thought were fine, like "they're pretty," "they read well."
But my brother, who works in human resources, told me those CVs aren't used anymore, because companies now run every CV through an AI called Citrus ATS.
But David showed me the solution.
There's a website where you upload your CV and it scores it, to see how likely it is to pass the ATS filters so companies can actually see it.
And look, as you can see, mine is really bad, but you can tap "improve" here and it improves it automatically.
Now it passes all the ATS filters.
verdict.hook_en: How I stopped being unemployed 🧚✨ / I literally applied to 1000 (I checked) 💀 / If your CV doesn't pass them, no HUMAN will even see your CV 💀💀💀
verdict.reason: The premise is the one N10 covers: lots of applications and no offers, because pretty Canva CVs don't get through the ATS and so no human ever sees them. The fix is uploading the CV to a site that scores it and improves it automatically. The brother in HR is a side detail in the middle of the video, not the hook, so it isn't N07.

Because they might look "presentable", but they don't pass the ATS check.
A perfect CV looks something like this.
But a friend of mine who works in HR recommended a website that can help you make the perfect CV.
This is the site, it's called Jobstep.io.
Basically, you just upload your CV and it analyzes it and scores it.
If the score comes out under 50%, like mine did, it gets rejected.
It's really easy to fix: you just follow the steps it suggests.
First it fixes the structure, and then you answer a few short questions the AI asks you, especially about your education and experience.
That way you'll now have a much better score, and the final result will look something like this.

verdict.english_script:
I recently got out of unemployment, and let me tell you how I did it.
My sister works in HR, and she told me that when they see a CV made in Canva, they literally throw it out without even reading it.
Why? Because these CVs don't get through ATS filters anymore. ATS is software companies use to check whether your profile is a good fit.
If they see it's from Canva or it doesn't have the specific keywords, they throw it out immediately.
So I asked her: "Hey, what's the solution to getting into those jobs?" Or to getting through the ATS filters.
And she told me: "Oh, I installed an app called Jobstep.io, and we're literally going to do this."
Here's the app, it's called Jobstep.io.
You just copy the link to the job you want, and it analyzes it right away and creates a CV and a cover letter for us.
It also tailors a CV for us.
And as you can see here, you really can get through the ATS filters: we've got 96%, and that's a good score.
And this is roughly what our CV looks like.
I hope you liked it.

verdict.english_script:
As a professional HR woman, I'll show you how to find a job.
Listen to me carefully: a CV I receive, name... little name, rejected.
Another CV I receive, we tear it up.
Also void.
All these cutesy little things you do, forget them.
Come on, they're not meant to look pretty and sweet here, with their icons, with their drawings, like this, their colors.
They don't work for me.
First of all, I don't see them.
There's no time for me to look at all of them, so I end up looking at the 5 best ones.
When an HR person receives 1,000 CVs, and I'm not saying per day, I'm saying per week.
Which is a realistic fact.
You can ask anyone you want.
You can't read them all, you don't have the time.
We put them into an AI system, we run them through filters, they're called ATS, and they cut the CVs that aren't relevant.
Because there are CVs that put way too much information on them that isn't needed for that specific position.
When you apply for a job, you have to make the application specific, with keywords that match the position we're looking to fill.
Otherwise it's for something else, not for this.
If you don't have experience in that specific position, don't put irrelevant stuff, it doesn't count either.
Also, the icons and all the things you add to make it look prettier, well, they make the AI system lag, so your CV won't get through no matter how hard you try.
Even if you deserve the job and have the qualifications, if you put irrelevant things and silly little icons, it doesn't get through, unfortunately.
So it's a shame to lose out.
A proper CV is this one.
And why is it proper?
Because it has everything in order, one by one, categorized.
The most important things are in black bold, so the eye lands there.
It's elegant, it's simple, and it's exactly about the position you applied for.
Because I know what it's like to go through having to make a CV, and it's very time-consuming to make a different one for each position, there's an app that can help you do it more easily and quickly.
You go to this site called Jobstep.
So, here, the position you want to apply for, let's add it, and it analyzes it with filters, ATS and keywords.
So let's build the CV step by step.
And here you have the CV I told you about.
Here you can also chat live and edit it depending on what else you want, what's missing, or what experience you might have forgotten, previous work, etc.
So you save it, and you can also send a personalized cover letter for that specific position, like this.
verdict.hook_en: How HR reacts to your CVs‼️ / As a professional HR woman, I'll show you how to find a job.
verdict.reason: Same story as 'HR hates these CVs': the creator rejects designed CVs one after another, explains that ATS can't read icons and graphics, so qualified people get filtered out before HR sees them, then shows the tool for a plain ATS-friendly CV. The HR-professional role-play is only a different packaging.

verdict.english_script:
Ranking job-search websites in Argentina: yes, no, or maybe?
CompuTrabajo? Yes: it has loads of listings across different fields and works mainly for customer service, logistics and production operator jobs.
LinkedIn? Maybe: it's a really good option for networking, but big companies usually rely heavily on ATS systems; you always have to keep your profile up to date.
Bumeran? No, I wouldn't put it among my first options if I'm trying to widen my chances.
That doesn't mean it has no good listings, but it depends a lot on the field and the profile.
Jobstep.io, yes: it's one of the most complete because, besides tailoring your CV to pass ATS filters, it also has a page where you can copy and paste different job listings you're interested in, and it helps you rework your CV and writes you a cover letter.
What site would you add to the ranking?

verdict.english_script:
Lie on your CV.
And I'll say it again: lie on your CV.
And no, I don't mean making up new positions you've never worked in.
I mean the small details that still make a difference.
Because I also had no idea what to put on my CV, until a friend of mine recommended a tool.
You pick a job offer and copy its link.
Then you go to a site like JobStep, click "New offer" and paste the link you copied.
And the program analyzes it from every angle.
Next, you upload your old CV to the program, and it suggests what you can change or improve in your CV.
That way your CV will be better matched to that specific job offer.
And seriously, it's hard to believe it's this simple.
And at the end you get a new, improved CV that jumped from 36 points to a score of 96 points, which is a really, really big jump.
So this site is seriously pretty good.
verdict.hook_en: Lie on your CV. And I'll say it again: lie on your CV.

verdict.english_script:
Now that I've left HR, I can tell you why your CVs are getting rejected.
As a former HR employee, today I'll admit something that still gives me a guilty conscience.
Did you know that as many as 80% of the CVs you send are never read by a human?
They're all rejected within seconds by software called ATS.
Now that I've left that job, I can say it plainly: if you want an interview invitation, you have to speak the system's language.
When I worked in HR, we checked whether candidates were tailoring their CVs to the job offer, and especially whether they were using JobStep.
Because it's exactly the keyword match in your CV that decides which CV ends up on top.
So if you haven't had a single interview invitation for a month, it's not your fault. It's your CV's fault, because it just doesn't get through the ATS filters.
So now I'll show you how to get through those filters.
Here you paste the job offer you want to apply for and press "Add offer".
Next, you upload your old CV.
And we check how well my CV matches this offer.
As you can see, the score is 45, so we need to fix that right away.
Now I'm chatting with the chat and telling it about my experience, and as you can see, my score is going up.
Once I'd done everything, I clicked "Next", and as you can see, my score is now 96%.
This is roughly what my CV looks like now, which means I got through the ATS filters and I'll finally be invited to a job interview.
